root_causes: The planner produced only a single planning step and then repeatedly issued the same high-level action (Explore[dining_room_1]) without updating the plan or reacting to environment changes.
Agent 1's action was repeatedly auto-filled as Wait[None] due to missing planner output for that agent, effectively leaving one agent idle for the entire visible segment.

There was no transition from exploration to object acquisition and placement; the system failed to detect completion of exploration or to trigger a new subgoal (e.g., locating plates, glasses, forks, then setting them).
The task-state tracking showed 2/10 propositions completed and never progressed, indicating that the planner was not monitoring or responding to partial progress toward the goal.

Action diversity and search were inadequate: the agent continued exploring the same room region instead of switching to targeted search, grasping, or placement actions once the dining room was sufficiently explored.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a multi-step planning loop that regularly re-plans based on updated world state, so the agent can switch from generic exploration to targeted fetch-and-place actions.
Ensure that both agents always receive explicit planned actions; eliminate reliance on auto-filled Wait[] by enforcing that the planner outputs actions for all agents each step.
Add clear termination or transition criteria for exploration (e.g., coverage thresholds or timeouts) that trigger a change to object search and manipulation behaviors.
Strengthen progress-aware planning: continuously track which propositions (plates, glasses, forks placed correctly) are satisfied and bias the policy toward actions that advance remaining subgoals.

Incorporate diversity and fallback strategies in action selection so the system stops repeating ineffective actions (e.g., repeated Explore in the same room) and tries alternative regions or action types.
Instrument debugging/metrics to detect stagnation (e.g., no new objects found or propositions completed over N steps) and force a planner reset or higher-level policy change.
overall_assessment: The execution stagnated in repetitive exploration with one agent idle, achieving only partial task completion and failing to transition to effective object placement. Planning and progress-tracking were insufficiently responsive to the environment, leading to low overall task performance.
task_instruction: Help me set the table for 2 people in the dining room. Place 2 plates, 2 glasses, and 2 forks at each setting, and make sure to place them next to each other.
